correctness.rationale: For xy=B(x,y)u, closure of any W is exactly u∈W or B restricted to W vanishes; the overlap for isotropic u is the totally isotropic Grassmannian of u-perp/Fu. Nondegenerate finite quadratic-space zero counts follow from a normalized additive-character Gauss sum, and incidence double counting proves all T_r without an unproved nonstandard enumeration lemma. The modularity obstruction is an explicit triple of subalgebras using normalized isotropic x outside span(u,w), available in at least q^(n-2)>1 ways; the dimension-two lattice is classified by its atoms. Direct multiplication/subspace RREF enumeration over F3,F5,F7,F9 reproduced all 75 independent parameter configurations (81,142 subspaces checked). The finite computations are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The central new mathematical statement is a full dimension-resolved, finite-field count of ordinary subalgebras for every nondegenerate evolution algebra with one-dimensional square, including the overlap correction when the distinguished square generator is isotropic, and the information recovered from the one-dimensional coefficient. Known bilinear classification does not itself provide this rank enumerator. Published solvable-case modularity is explicitly acknowledged as already proved; it is not an originality assertion. value.rationale: The full rank-generating count of ordinary subalgebras of a natural, infinite family of finite nonassociative evolution algebras is a motivated exact structural invariant, not a chosen small parameter. The formula combines a Gaussian subspace interval with a classical orthogonal polar Grassmannian and corrects their nontrivial overlap when the square generator is isotropic; every coefficient is explicit for arbitrary odd q and n. In addition, N1 recovers the Witt type in even dimension and whether the generator has zero square, giving interpretable structural content; a sharp non-modularity witness completes the lattice picture in the non-solvable range. It concretely addresses a recent stated lattice-reconstruction direction. Novelty is not based merely on a correct computation.
